text:
maria: quick q — console p99 for /v1/generate jumps when I slice by edge=eu-west-1 but p50 stays flat. anyone seen provenance flips like this? example snapshot: global p50 120ms p95 280ms p99 900ms; eu-west-1 p50 118ms p95 290ms p99 1.8s :confused:

devon: do you mean the console chart or the raw analytics rollup query?

maria: console chart (latency panel). no deploys or incidents around that window.

kevin: first thought = sampling instability when you apply a tight slice. how many samples for that edge slice in the window?

maria: sample count drops from ~200k -> ~3.2k across the same timeframe.

sam: 3.2k typically ok for p99 but if there are a couple heavy outliers it can blow up. do we apply a different smoothing/aggregation path for small slices?

devon: console uses tdigest rollups for most rollups, but we have a heuristic that swaps to histogram fallback for mid-size slices. @observability-bot can you confirm exact thresholds?

observability-bot: heuristic summary: tdigest rollup used when slice_count >= 10000; histogram fallback used when 1000 <= slice_count < 10000; raw-sample summary used when slice_count < 1000. (source: docs/telemetry/rollups.md)

kevin: that explains a lot — the histogram fallback has coarse 50ms buckets. a single 1.8s outlier will sit in the top bucket and push p99 dramatically once sample count drops.

maria: so the UI p99 is showing the histogram-derived percentile which is sensitive to bucket edges and outliers. suggestion: surface the provenance (tdigest/histogram/raw) next to the value.

devon: also worth checking if the slice includes fallback routes. routing fallbacks can add a few very high-latency requests. were routes tagged separately in that slice?

maria: filter was edge=eu-west-1 + endpoint=/v1/generate only, so it may mix primary + fallback routes.

sam: quick actionable checks: run analytics query grouping by sample_origin and verify p99 per origin. something like:
```
SELECT minute, count(*) AS n, pctl(0.99, latency_ms) AS p99, sample_origin
FROM requests
WHERE edge='eu-west-1' AND endpoint='/v1/generate'
GROUP BY minute, sample_origin
ORDER BY minute DESC
LIMIT 60;
```

kevin: and also run raw histogram buckets to see bucket population: `SELECT histogram(latency_ms, 50) FROM ...` to confirm top-bucket mass.

maria: running now, will paste top 5 minutes.

maria: pasted results — p99 spikes align with sample_origin='fallback' slices; fallback rows are ~0.6-0.9% of traffic but contain latencies 1.2s-2.1s. when histogram fallback is used, that small tail dominates computed p99.

devon: ok. short-term: UI should show provenance badge (tdigest/histogram/raw) + sample_count + top sample_origin. that lets on-call decide if p99 is meaningful.

kevin: medium-term: revisit the heuristic thresholds. maybe require a minimal top-percentile sample count or compute an interpolated percentile across origins to avoid single-origin dominance.

sam: could also add a console tooltip: "p99 provenance: histogram (bucket_size=50ms), sample_count=3200, dominant_origin=fallback (0.7%)"

maria: will open a console ticket with repro steps and screenshots. tagging: @devon @kevin @sam.

devon: thanks — also add the analytics query and paste the raw histogram so platform team can reproduce.

kevin: low-effort hotfix: show sample_count and sample_origin breakdown inline. long fix: better rollup blending logic.

maria: noted. I'll create the ticket and attach the queries + sample rows. closing here for now :thumbsup:
